_readme: Evergreen guide per month (1-12), shown on singapore-this-month.html alongside that month's dated events (YYYY-MM.json). Festival dates that move every year are described without exact dates here; the monthly data file has the exact ones.

1.weather: Northeast monsoon: 24–31°C, frequent afternoon showers and some rainy days, often a little cooler and breezy.
typical: Pongal in Little India, usually mid-January
Chinese New Year preparations and the Chinatown light-up (Chinese New Year falls in late January or February)
Thaipusam procession from Little India (January or February)
tips: Hotels near Chinatown fill up before Chinese New Year
Carry an umbrella every day

2.weather: Usually the driest, breeziest month: 24–31°C with fewer showers.
typical: Chinese New Year celebrations (late January or February), with River Hongbao and the Chingay Parade around this time
Valentine's Day dining and rooftop bars
tips: Many small shops and hawker stalls close for a few days over Chinese New Year
Great month for outdoor sights and the Southern Ridges walk

3.weather: Hot and fairly dry early in the month: 25–32°C, with thunderstorms returning towards April.
typical: Mid-year school break for Singapore schools in mid-March
Ramadan bazaars in some years (Ramadan moves about 11 days earlier each year)
tips: Attractions are busier during the March school holidays
Stay hydrated; afternoons are hot

4.weather: Inter-monsoon: hot (25–32°C) with short, heavy afternoon thunderstorms.
typical: Hari Raya Puasa light-up in Geylang Serai in years when it falls in March or April
Good Friday and Easter events
tips: Plan outdoor sights for the morning
Lightning alerts can pause outdoor rides and pools

5.weather: One of the hottest months: 26–32°C, humid, with afternoon storms.
typical: Vesak Day (May or June) at temples across the island
Hari Raya celebrations in some years
tips: Indian summer holidays start, so flights from India get pricier
Indoor attractions are your friend in the afternoon heat

6.weather: Southwest monsoon begins: 26–31°C, generally drier with early-morning squalls.
typical: Singapore school holidays all month
Hari Raya Haji in some years
Great Singapore Sale season in malls
tips: Universal Studios and the zoo are busiest; book fixed-date tickets
Peak season for Indian families visiting

7.weather: Southwest monsoon: 26–31°C, relatively dry with occasional morning squalls.
typical: Singapore Food Festival (usually around July)
National Day Parade rehearsals and fireworks previews on some Saturdays
tips: Good value month once Indian summer holidays end
Great time for Sentosa beaches

8.weather: Southwest monsoon: 26–31°C, mostly dry, occasional haze in some years.
typical: National Day on 9 August: parade, fireworks and the city in red and white
Hungry Ghost Festival performances (August or September)
tips: Marina Bay is very crowded around 9 August
Check the haze forecast if you have breathing issues

9.weather: Late southwest monsoon: 25–31°C, warm, occasional haze.
typical: Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix night race (usually September or early October)
Mid-Autumn Festival lanterns in Chinatown and Gardens by the Bay (September or October)
Halloween Horror Nights at Universal Studios starts around late September
tips: Hotel prices around Marina Bay jump on Grand Prix weekend
Lantern displays look best after dark

typical: Deepavali light-up and bazaars in Little India (Deepavali falls in October or November)
Halloween Horror Nights at Universal Studios
Mid-Autumn celebrations in some years
tips: Little India is busiest on weekends before Deepavali
Carry an umbrella in the afternoon

11.weather: Start of the northeast monsoon: 24–31°C, wetter, with frequent showers.
typical: Deepavali in some years
Orchard Road Christmas light-up begins in mid to late November
Singapore school holidays begin in late November
tips: Year-end sales start
Book December trips and tickets early

12.weather: Northeast monsoon: 24–31°C, the wettest stretch, with heavy showers that usually pass in an hour or two.
typical: Orchard Road Christmas light-up and festive events across the city
Christmas markets and festive shows at Gardens by the Bay and Sentosa
New Year's Eve fireworks at Marina Bay
tips: Peak season: book flights and hotels early
Plan outdoor sights for mornings and keep indoor backups
